summary: Indian IT, Day 241. The feared US-demand profit warning has not come; instead HCLTech raised guidance and TCS beat, and Nifty IT had its best week since 2008. Infosys cut FY27 revenue guidance to 1–2% on 23 Oct — the nearest miss — and the US suspended the big four from the PERM green-card programme. IT is the sector holding the Nifty up.

US Labor Department suspended Infosys/TCS/Wipro/HCL from the PERM green-card programme (8 Oct). Nifty IT +8.2% since 13 Oct (best week since Apr 2008 to 16 Oct). (CONFIRMED results; intel IND-A9)

**No profit warning — the opposite.** TCS Q2 FY27 (8 Oct): revenue $7,642mn (+0.2% QoQ; CC +0.5% QoQ / +2.8% YoY), margin 24.0%, TCV $9.6bn, annualised AI revenue $3.1bn; shares +5.5% (9 Oct). HCLTech (12 Oct): CC +2.6% YoY, PAT +21.2%, **FY27 CC guidance raised to 2.5–4% (from 1–4%)**; stock +9% to ₹1,326 (13 Oct); Nifty IT +5.2% to 29,830. Rupee does much of the INR growth (TCS INR +11.2% vs CC +2.8%). Wipro 15 Oct (guided −1.5% to +0.5% CC); Infosys 23 Oct. Sector still ~−23% YTD. — CONFIRMED (company releases).

**IT led Tuesday's open (with HDFC Bank) as the 'dollar earner' hedge on ₹96 — then was overwhelmed by oil/yields. Second-order: the Fed hike raises US recession odds (CBO: war +0.5pp PCE), the standing headwind for IT demand. No company-specific news. (HDFC Sky) — REPORTED.**

IT sold with the Nifty on US-rates/recession risk (a Fed hike into an oil shock) — 14 of 16 sectors down w/w; no Tata/TCS succession update found this sweep (the 12-Aug Chandrasekaran resignation thread is UNRESOLVED in the graph, not resolved). (Mint; markets.md)

Indian IT ROUTED — Infosys/TCS led the decline that snapped the Nifty's 5-day streak (19 Jun), on the hawkish Fed's US-recession/IT-spend implications. The fed->indian-it channel is now the dominant India drag, distinct from the (resolved) crisis. ~5% crisis-linked; this is a US-rates story. CONFIRMED.

Indian IT the main Nifty drag on 11 Jun (Infosys -2.25%) on US-recession/CPI worry -- the sector most exposed to the US macro deterioration (CPI 4.2%, December-hike repricing, recession framing) rather than to the Gulf kinetics. The transmission to India is via the US demand/rates channel, not the war.

**THE AI-CAPEX DOUBT WENT MAINSTREAM — DOUBLE-EDGED FOR INDIAN IT SERVICES; THE 12.5% SECTION 301 TARIFF REMAINS A CONTESTABLE PROPOSAL INDIA IS NEGOTIATING.** The 5-June US session cracked the crowded AI/semi trade hard (Broadcom AI-guidance miss + hot May jobs 172K vs ~85K -> SMH -9.2%, Nasdaq -4%, VIX +39.7% to ~21.5) — a rates/AI de-risking. For Indian IT services this is DOUBLE-EDGED: the AI-builders trade (the engine of the 'AI-flows-bypass-Indian-services' overhang) is the one cracking, which marginally relieves that overhang; but the same hot-jobs/higher-for-longer rates read carries a US-demand/recession scare that is a headwind for discretionary IT spend. The continued FII/IT/oil drag persists. The US Section 301 12.5% tariff on India remains a PROPOSAL (within a ~54-economy action; comments ~22 Jun, hearings 7 Jul, decision late-Jun/Jul; India negotiating it into the trade pact) — a non-oil headwind that does NOT reverse on a Hormuz deal but is contingent/contestable, not levied. The structural cycle-bear is unchanged; the profit-warning trigger stays watching (no company guidance cut).

recent_signals.headline: **THE RUPEE-REVENUE TAILWIND FLIPPED — A NEW 12.5% US SECTION 301 TARIFF DROVE AN 'IT STOCK SHOCK' COMPONENT OF THE 2-3 JUNE INDIA SELLOFF.** USTR's proposed 12.5% tariff on India (vs 10% for EU/UK/Canada/Mexico) surfaced as a named driver of the 2 June rupee/Nifty weakness; for Indian IT it inverted the prior 'weak rupee = exporter tailwind' read into a US tariff/demand-risk headwind (the 'IT stock shock'). The structural bear (AI flows bypassing Indian services for the Korea/Taiwan/US stack) now carries a tariff/earnings overhang on top. India is seeking bilateral resolution; until then it does NOT reverse on a Hormuz deal. Profit-warning trigger stays watching (price/tariff-driven, not a company guidance cut).

IT is DISPERSING, not re-rating — a correction to the 17 Jul 'decent earnings season' framing. **Wipro MISSED and guided down**: net profit Rs3,356 cr flat YoY and -4.7% QoQ; revenue Rs24,479 cr +10.6% YoY but IT services revenue +1% YoY and **-1.4% QoQ**; margin **-130bps to 16.0%** on wage hikes and AI investment, with management conceding the 17-18% margin aspiration is out of reach 'at least over the next few quarters'; **Q2 FY27 guidance -1.5% to +0.5% QoQ constant currency, i.e. a CONTRACTING midpoint.** Large deal bookings were the one bright spot at $1.63bn, +12.9% QoQ across 13 deals. Stock fell ~2%. Against that, TCS and Tech Mahindra (net profit Rs1,465 cr, +28.4% YoY) beat. LTIMindtree had not reported in-window. The sector is carrying the index on the winners while the laggards guide down. CONFIRMED.
